latest_nl_proof: Because j/n <= x < (j+1)/n and n is positive, multiplying the inequality by n preserves the order and gives j <= nx < j+1. Now set t = nx - j. Subtracting j from the displayed inequality yields 0 <= t < 1. Also nx = j + t, so dividing by n gives x = (j+t)/n. The affine reconstruction map on the cell [j/n,(j+1)/n) is exactly T_{n,j}(u) = (j+u)/n, hence x = T_{n,j}(t).
statement_nl: Let n be a positive integer and j an integer with 0 <= j <= n - 1. If x is a real number with j/n <= x < (j + 1)/n, then t = n*x - j satisfies 0 <= t < 1 and x = T_{n,j}(t).

domain_restrictions: n is a positive integer (so n is at least 1, and division by n is valid over reals)
j is an integer satisfying 0 <= j <= n - 1
x is a real number satisfying j/n <= x < (j+1)/n
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all positive integers n and all integers j with 0 <= j <= n - 1, for all real x with j/n <= x < (j+1)/n, if t is defined by t = n*x - j, then 0 <= t < 1 and x equals T_{n,j}(t) (the reconstruction of x from t in that subinterval).
quantifier_order: for all n in positive integers
for all j in integers with 0 <= j <= n - 1
for all x in real numbers with j/n <= x and x < (j+1)/n

variables.name: n
variables.role: mesh parameter; used in interval endpoints and in formula for t

variables.name: j
variables.role: index selecting subinterval; constrained by 0 <= j <= n - 1

variables.name: t
variables.role: derived parameter defined by t = n*x - j

witness_dependencies: t depends on x (and on n and j) through the definition t = n*x - j
T_{n,j}(t) depends on n, j, and the derived value t
